title: How to record product demos without exposing customer data
summary: Learn how to demo your product without exposing customer data. Use dummy data or blur sensitive information in your product demos
body_markdown:
## Why customer data ends up in demo videos


Customer data usually enters a demo video when someone records directly in a production account or customer sandbox. Under time pressure, opening an existing account feels faster than creating a demo tenant with realistic records. The interface already contains populated dashboards and believable activity, but every visible record can carry private information into the recording.


Production screens can reveal data beyond the feature being demonstrated. A search field may suggest customer emails, while a billing page may expose payment details. Notifications can also appear during recording and display names, ticket text, or account activity that the presenter never intended to show. Even a customer sandbox may contain real records, credentials, or integrations that pull information from live systems.


A safer recording workflow starts with prevention. You should stage a clean environment and populate it with synthetic data before recording. After capture, you should inspect the footage and redact any sensitive details that still appeared. A final privacy review then checks the full frame, including notifications, browser tabs, and background windows, before publication.


## Why synthetic demo data beats blurring real data


Synthetic demo data prevents exposure because real customer information never enters the recording. A staged account can use fabricated names, example.com email addresses, invented invoice numbers, and dummy payment details while preserving the screens and states the demo needs. Viewers still see a realistic workflow, but an overlooked field cannot reveal customer data.


Blurring real data depends on finding every appearance during editing. An email address might appear in a profile field, then surface again in a search result or notification. A reviewer may miss a single frame during a page transition. The raw recording also retains the original information until someone edits or deletes it.


A synthetic dataset should be generated independently rather than copied and lightly scrambled from production records. Consistent relationships make the data believable. For example, the same fabricated company can appear across its account, invoices, and support tickets. You can also seed specific conditions such as an overdue payment or unresolved ticket without involving a real customer.


Masking remains useful when the demo must show a production-only workflow or when real data appears unexpectedly.[Clueso](https://www.clueso.io/) can blur sensitive on-screen information and replace exposed values with synthetic data inside the video workflow. You should still restrict access to the raw recording and delete it according to your retention policy, since redaction protects the finished video rather than the source file.


## Building a clean demo environment before you hit record


A dedicated demo tenant keeps customer information out of the recording from the start. Build it separately instead of cloning a production account, since a clone can preserve names, files, and hidden metadata. Match the production interface and feature settings closely enough for the workflow you plan to show, and pick[screen recording software](https://www.clueso.io/solutions/screen-recording-software) that gives you control over exactly what the capture includes.


1. **Create accounts for each role in the demo.** Use a company-owned domain and invented names, such asmaya@northstar-demo.example . Give each account only the permissions required for the recording. Check profile photos, account menus, and user lists because those areas can expose whoever created the tenant.
2. **Seed realistic dummy records.** Add fabricated customers, tickets, projects, or invoices that support the exact story in your script. Keep the records internally consistent. For example, an invoice should reference the same dummy company and contact shown elsewhere. Use clearly fake payment details and never copy production records as templates.
3. **Disable connections to live systems.** Disconnect shared inboxes, CRM syncs, payment processors, analytics feeds, and webhooks before recording. An integration can import a real contact or trigger a notification even when every visible record started as dummy data. Replace required connections with sandbox accounts where possible.
4. **Prepare each screen before recording.** Open the correct record, set filters, clear recent searches, and close unrelated browser tabs. Turn off desktop notifications and messaging previews. Reset the demo tenant to a saved starting state before every take so earlier attempts do not change counts or activity histories.
5. **Run the full script once without recording.** Watch menus, search suggestions, autofill fields, and error messages for unexpected data. Confirm that every click stays inside the demo tenant. If the walkthrough requires a production screen, identify it in advance so you can apply redaction or synthetic replacement during editing rather than discovering the exposure after publication.


Once the environment is ready, an[AI screen recorder](https://www.clueso.io/features/screen-recorder) that captures cleanly and hands off straight into editing saves a re-record if something still slips through.


## Where sensitive data leaks in during recording


A staged demo environment can still display sensitive data through interface elements that sit outside the planned click path. Keep the entire screen in view while recording, including navigation menus, browser chrome, and temporary messages.


- **Emails and account identifiers** often appear in profile menus, assignee fields, search suggestions, and browser autofill. Watch for real domains, usernames, customer IDs, and email addresses.
- **Customer and employee names** can surface in activity feeds, comments, ticket histories, and recently viewed lists. Seeded records do not protect the recording if a connected feature retrieves live user details.
- **Billing and payment information** may appear on subscription pages, invoices, receipts, and checkout screens. Check for card digits, billing addresses, transaction IDs, and downloadable document previews before opening each view.
- **API keys and access tokens** can remain visible in settings pages, command examples, or copied text. Even partially hidden credentials may reveal enough information to identify an account or internal environment.
- **Notification pop-ups and toasts** can expose data without any deliberate action. An incoming email preview, chat message, calendar reminder, or product alert may display a real name or account detail for only a few seconds.
- **Background tabs and system surfaces** can enter the frame when you switch windows, upload a file, or open a browser dialog. Tab titles, bookmarks, filenames, desktop notifications, and recent-file lists all deserve the same attention as the product interface.


Treat these leak points as an active recording checklist. Automated detection and redaction can catch missed elements later, but knowing where exposure occurs helps you avoid capturing unnecessary customer data in the first place.

## How do I hide sensitive information in screen recordings and screenshots?


To hide sensitive information in screenshots or blur video content, start with the capture controls built into your operating system. Screenshot markup and editing tools on macOS and Windows let you crop, cover, or otherwise obscure private details. These tools work for occasional screenshots, but editing every image manually takes time and makes it easy to miss a frame in a video.


Before recording, turn on Do Not Disturb or a focus mode at the operating system level. This prevents email previews, chat messages, calendar reminders, and other notifications from appearing unexpectedly.


Choose window capture instead of full-desktop capture when the walkthrough stays inside one application. Limiting the capture area reduces the chance that background tabs, filenames, taskbars, or unrelated windows will enter the recording.


Clueso is a direct fit when you need more than manual per-screenshot editing. Its native redaction workflow can blur sensitive information on any screen in a video and replace exposed values with generated synthetic data. These capabilities work directly inside the screen-recording and video-production workflow rather than serving only as finishing tools for a polished export.

## How do I set up a demo environment with realistic dummy data instead of faking it manually?


Set up a dedicated demo environment to anonymize data before you record. Follow the preparation process in the section above on building a clean demo environment, including separating the tenant from production, disabling live integrations, and seeding the states required by your script.


The slow approach is to invent every name, email address, invoice number, and related record by hand. You also have to keep those values consistent across profiles, tables, billing pages, and support histories so the demo remains believable.


[Clueso](https://www.clueso.io/) offers a faster alternative inside the video and screen-recording workflow. It detects sensitive elements in a screen recording and lets you either blur them or replace them with generated synthetic data. You can apply those protections to any screen before exporting the finished video.


Use blur when viewers do not need to read the hidden value. API keys, payment details, account numbers, and notification pop-ups usually fit this case. Clueso obscures the selected area while leaving the surrounding interface visible, so you can blur video content without covering the full screen.


Use synthetic replacement when the visible value helps explain the workflow. Clueso can swap a real customer name or email address for a fabricated one, which keeps form fields, tables, and account pages readable. The generated data preserves the context of the demonstration without displaying the original customer information.


Native redaction also keeps privacy work inside the video production workflow. After treating sensitive areas, you can use Clueso to enhance the script, add an AI voiceover, generate captions, and polish the raw screen recording, the same steps covered in[scaling product demo video production without a video team](https://www.clueso.io/blog/product-demo-video-production) .


## Privacy review checklist before you publish


Treat the privacy review as a final verification step after staging, redaction, and editing. Review the exported file rather than the editing preview, since cropping and rendering can reveal content near the frame edges.


- Play the video at full resolution and pause on every form, table, search result, and account page.
- Confirm that every email address uses dummy data or remains fully blurred.
- Check names, usernames, avatars, account IDs, and customer references for real identities.
- Inspect billing screens for card details, bank information, invoice numbers, addresses, and transaction records.
- Scan settings, developer tools, and URL fields for API keys, access tokens, passwords, and private links.
- Replay transitions slowly to catch notification pop-ups and toast messages that appear for only a few frames.
- Verify that each blur or synthetic replacement stays in place during scrolling, zooming, and cursor movement.
- Scrub the full screen for browser tab titles, background tabs, bookmarks, desktop notifications, and taskbar previews.
- Ask someone who did not edit the video to complete one final viewing before publication.


A failed check should send the affected clip back for correction. You usually need to fix one section rather than record the entire demo again.

## FAQs


**How do you blur part of a video?**


Selective blurring covers a sensitive area while leaving the rest of the frame visible. Clueso lets you blur video elements such as emails, names, payment details, and API keys within the editing workflow. You can protect private information without exporting the recording to a separate redaction tool.


**Should product demos use synthetic or real customer data?**


Synthetic demo data uses fabricated names, accounts, and records that resemble realistic product activity. Clueso can generate synthetic data to replace sensitive information when a recording includes production screens. Fabricated data reduces the risk of exposing customer information that an editor might miss.


**Should someone review a demo after applying automated redaction?**


A privacy review checks every frame for information that automated redaction or staging may have missed. Clueso handles blurring and synthetic replacement, while the reviewer verifies notifications, background tabs, and brief screen transitions. A final review catches unexpected content before publication.
